identity.title: ALMACAL I: First Dual-band Number Counts from a Deep and Wide ALMA Submillimeter Survey, Free from Cosmic Variance

paper_type_evidence.quote: We have exploited ALMA calibration observations to carry out a novel, wide and deep submm survey, almacal.

targets.name: 69 ALMA calibrator fields (e.g. J1058+0133, J0108+0135, J1744-3116)

redshift_or_distance.value: calibrator z listed in table; DSFG redshifts unknown

question.value: Can archival ALMA calibrator observations be combined into a deep, wide submm survey to detect faint DSFGs and measure cumulative number counts in bands 6 and 7?

evidence.quote: Gathering together data acquired during multiple visits to many ALMA calibrators, it is possible to reach noise levels which allow the detection of faint dusty, star-forming galaxies (DSFGs) over a significant area.

bands.value: Band 6 (~250 GHz, 1.2 mm) and Band 7 (~345 GHz, 870 um)

evidence.loc: 2 Extracting and calibrating ALMA calibrator data
evidence.quote: we retrieved data in ALMA bands 6 (B6, around 250 GHz or 1.2 mm) and 7 (B7, around 345 GHz or 870 $\mu$m)

evidence.loc: 2 Extracting and calibrating ALMA calibrator data
evidence.quote: most of our ALMA maps have sub-arcsec resolution

sensitivity.value: rms ~25 uJy/beam in the deepest maps; typically ~30 uJy/beam

evidence.quote: reaching depths of $\sim 25 \, {\rm \mu Jy \, beam^{-1}}$ at sub-arcsec resolution

pi_or_archival_as_stated.value: Public archival calibrator data observed before July 2015; proprietary data obtained via helpdesk request

evidence.loc: 2 Extracting and calibrating ALMA calibrator data
evidence.quote: We first used the ALMA calibrator archive to find all calibrators observed prior to 2015 July as part of science projects that passed quality control.

what.value: Composite LESS SMG SED used for the band 870 um to 1.2 mm conversion and the SED templates

evidence.quote: The counts have been converted from 870 $\mu$m to 1.2 mm using the composite SMG SED from the LESS survey (cite: Swinbank2014MNRAS.438.1267S), redshifted to $z = 2.3$

what.value: Literature ALMA number counts for comparison

evidence.quote: Previous results based on ALMA data, from (cite: Karim2013MNRAS.432....2K), (cite: Simpson2015ApJ...807..128S), (cite: Hatsukade2013ApJ...769L..27H), (cite: Ono2014ApJ...795....5O) and (cite: Fujimoto2015arXiv150503523F) are also shown.

pipeline_or_manual.value: Delivered calibration reapplied to bandpass calibrators; pseudo-continuum self-calibration with a point-source uv model; statwt reweighting

evidence.loc: 2 Extracting and calibrating ALMA calibrator data
evidence.quote: we needed to recover the correct flux density scale of the bandpass calibrators from the flux tables in the data delivery packages and re-apply the calibration tables to the calibrators.

self_calibration.value: Two rounds (phase, then amplitude+phase), solution interval = integration time, point-source model fitted in uv

evidence.loc: 2 Extracting and calibrating ALMA calibrator data
evidence.quote: Two rounds of self-calibration were applied, at first only in phase, then in both amplitude and phase, both with a solution interval equal to the integration time.

task.value: CASA clean, per scheduling block; then concat of all data per calibrator per band

evidence.loc: 2 Extracting and calibrating ALMA calibrator data
evidence.quote: The calibrator-subtracted visibilities for every SB were then imaged individually, without combining data for a given calibrator, using the clean task.

masking.value: Cleaning window radius 1.5x PB FWHM (23'' B6, 17'' B7), cleaned to the rms of the dirty image; 1.5'' box around detections for flux measurement

evidence.loc: 2 Extracting and calibrating ALMA calibrator data
evidence.quote: we defined a cleaning window of radius 1.5$\times$ the expected fwhm of the PB (23$''$ and 17$''$ in B6 and B7, respectively) in each band

primary_beam_correction.value: impbcor after cleaning; source detection done before PB correction

evidence.quote: After cleaning, the maps were corrected for PB attenuation using impbcor

findings_qualitative.value: Faintest DSFGs would be missed by the deepest Herschel surveys

claims.hypothesis: Calibrator fields can yield a deep, wide submm survey of faint DSFGs
claims.experiment: Combine archival B6/B7 calibrator data for 69 pointings, subtract calibrator, detect at >=5 sigma
claims.result: 8 (B6) and 11 (B7) DSFGs found, down to ~0.2 mJy at 1.2 mm
claims.finding: The method works; dynamic range is not a strong limitation

evidence.loc: 2 Extracting and calibrating ALMA calibrator data
evidence.quote: We conclude, therefore, that the presence of the calibrator in the middle of the image has not proved to be a strong limitation.

claims.hypothesis: Faint number counts agree with previous ALMA estimates
claims.experiment: Cumulative counts corrected for completeness and area, compared with the literature
claims.result: Counts lower by a factor of at least 2
claims.finding: Earlier counts, based on lower-SNR thresholds, are probably overestimated

evidence.quote: The counts are lower than reported previously by a factor of at least $2\times$.

why_this_method.value: Conservative 5 sigma threshold to avoid spurious sources so that multi-band follow-up is reliable

evidence.quote: we have opted to be conservative – to reduce as much as possible the contamination from spurious sources

limitations_admitted.value: Possible jet contamination and a possible low-level bias from over-densities around calibrators

evidence.quote: we concede that selection of DSFGs around bright submm calibrators may be biased at a low level

referee_caveats_inferred: Small samples (8 and 11 sources) give large Poisson errors
The 870 um to 1.2 mm conversion depends on an assumed SED and z=2.3
Calibrator-subtraction residuals could cause spurious detections
